hydraulics.cylinder_force.title: Hydraulic cylinder extension and retraction force (F = p·A)
assumptions: Double-acting cylinder; extension acts on the full bore, retraction on the annulus (bore minus rod). Friction and seal drag neglected.
method_references: F = p·A; annulus area = π(D² − d²)/4

hydraulics.cylinder_speed.title: Cylinder extension and retraction speeds from flow rate (v = Q/A)
assumptions: Incompressible flow; extension uses the full bore area, retraction the annulus (bore minus rod). Leakage neglected. The rod must be smaller than the bore; when d ≈ D the annulus vanishes and the retraction speed is unbounded (a warning is raised).
method_references: Q = A·v; bore area πD²/4, annulus area π(D² − d²)/4

hydraulics.pump.title: Pump displacement, flow, efficiencies and drive torque

variables.name: n
variables.desc: pump shaft speed in rev/s (Hz); 1500 rpm = 25 rev/s

assumptions: Displacement per revolution, so flow = D·n with n in rev/s. Volumetric efficiency accounts for internal leakage; overall = volumetric × mechanical. The shaft torque is the ideal D·Δp/(2π) divided by the mechanical efficiency; shaft power = T·2π·n = Δp·Q_th/ηm.
method_references: Q_th = D·n; ηv = Q_act/Q_th; ηo = ηv·ηm; T = D·Δp/(2π·ηm)

hydraulics.hydraulic_motor.title: Hydraulic motor torque and speed

variables.name: n
variables.desc: actual shaft speed ηv·Q/D_m in rev/s (Hz)

assumptions: Ideal torque T = D·Δp/(2π) (the 2π converts per-revolution displacement to per-radian work); actual torque reduced by the mechanical efficiency. Theoretical speed n_th = Q/D is reduced by internal leakage: actual speed n = ηv·Q/D.
method_references: T = D·Δp/(2π); n_th = Q/D; n = ηv·Q/D

hydraulics.accumulator.title: Gas-charged accumulator volume (polytropic, Boyle when n = 1)
assumptions: Polytropic gas law P·V^n = const with ABSOLUTE pressures (gauge inputs shift the compression ratio and give roughly −4 % volume errors). n = 1 for slow (isothermal) cycling, n = 1.4 for fast (adiabatic) cycling of air. Precharge must be below the minimum system pressure (P0 < P1 < P2, enforced); the usable volume is V1 − V2.

hydraulics.line_pressure_drop.title: Line pressure drop (Darcy–Weisbach)

variables.name: f
variables.desc: Darcy friction factor (user input; see fluid_dynamics)

assumptions: Darcy–Weisbach loss with the Darcy friction factor f (not Fanning, which is f/4). Minor (fitting) losses add via K·ρv²/2.

hydraulics.hydraulic_power_heat.title: Hydraulic power and heat generation
assumptions: Hydraulic power P = p·Q; the inefficiency (1 − η) of that power is dissipated as heat into the oil (sizing the cooler).

hydraulics.pneumatic_consumption.title: Pneumatic cylinder air consumption and free air delivery

variables.name: V_cycle
variables.desc: working volume per full cycle (out + return) at pressure

variables.name: V_free
variables.desc: free air delivered per cycle (at p_atm and T_ref)

assumptions: Isothermal Boyle expansion of the compressed working volume to atmospheric pressure; one cycle = one extension plus one retraction. The temperature ratio TR = T_ref/T_supply converts the delivered air to a reference temperature (set 1 to ignore temperature); FAD is typically quoted at standard reference conditions.

source.derivation: A_bore = pi (2 in)^2/4 = 3.141593 in^2; A_ann = pi (4 - 1)/4 = 2.356194 in^2; F_ext = 1500 psi x 3.141593 in^2 = 4712.39 lbf; F_ret = 1500 x 2.356194 = 3534.29 lbf (imperial case exercising unit conversion)
V_free = V_cycle x (p_abs/p_atm) x TR = 3.61283e-4 x 6.92154 x 1.2 = 3.00076e-3; Q_free = 3.00076e-3 x 0.5 = 1.50038e-3 (temperature-ratio option)
